Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44181 of 2022
Applicant :- Ramkishan

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Arti Bhatt,Nishad Ramjanki,Pradeep Kumar,

Sabhajeet Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vipin Kumar Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
Applicant - Ramkishan has approached this Court for bail in Case Crime No. 93 of 2019 under Sections 452, 376, 354-Ka, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Chandpur, District- Fatehpur.

Learned A.G.A.-I for State, at the outset, on instructions, submits that applicant has criminal history of six cases prior to lodging of F.I.R. and thereafter he is also involved in three other cases.

It has been brought on record that applicant has long criminal history wherein he is facing allegations of rape, kidnapping, fraud, cheating, offence under Excise Act and offence under Damage to Public Property Act.
It has also been submitted by learned A.G.A.-I that applicant is a person of powerful nature and nobody wants to speak against him.

Sri Sabhajeet, learned counsel for applicant submits that he is related to victim as chacha and it is a case of false implication; the alleged occurrence took place in the year 2018, however, F.I.R. was Ramkishan vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199293465/
1 lodged in the year 2019 and as such there is a delay of about nine months which has not been explained; in order to make out a strong case, for the first time, victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. disclosed date of occurrence of rape which appears to be afterthought; he further submits that there was enmity since 2013 and family of victim was looking opportunity to falsely implicate the applicant; applicant is a very respected person and allegation of being a powerful person is absolutely incorrect; learned counsel has referred certain affidavits of villagers with a declaration that it was a false case; applicant has a defence of alibi also; therefore, applicant,
who is in jail since 23.07.2022, may be released on bail.

Above submissions are opposed by S/Sri Paritosh Malviya, learned A.G.A.-I for State and Vipin Kumar, learned counsel for informant and have referred long criminal history of applicant and that statement of victim has not been recorded as well as that defence in regard to alibi is not based on any cogent evidence.
In the present case, it appears that applicant has taken advantage of his family relationship with victim and allegedly committed repeated rape to victim.

There is a long criminal history of applicant which has not been denied which involved criminal cases of rape, forgery, cheating, kidnapping,
offence under Excise Act as well as offence under Damage to Public Property Act.
Statement of victim remained consistent even in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
she has disclosed specific date also.

The submission of learned counsel for applicant in regard to alibi cannot be considered at this stage and affidavits referred by learned counsel for applicant have no legal consequence as well as document referred does not indicate that he was confined to bed or was admitted in any hospital.

So far as submission in regard to reputation is concerned, evidence collected is not supportive as well as taking note that statement of victim has not been recorded during trial, therefore, in case of bail, it is very likelihood that applicant will try to influence the victim.

In these circumstances,
prayer for bail cannot be accepted, hence, rejected.

However, this application is disposed of with a direction that learned trial Court shall take all endeavour to record statement of victim expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months from today, if there is no legal impediment and thereafter applicant will have liberty to file fresh bail application before learned trial Court.
Order Date :- 22.3.2023
